judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short interpretive note that masculine terms include all employees; the wording is plain and creates no operative right whose boundary could be disputed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is a construction aid rather than an operative term and does not collide with any provision; checked against Section 2 and Section 4, which use masculine forms throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The phrase 'or its successor' is undefined and could be read broadly or narrowly, though the parties themselves are named with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 19 states the Agreement is to be treated as an individual agreement between the Union and each Publisher, which sits uneasily with the Association-as-agent framing here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Approximately fifty miles' and 'bounded approximately as follows' are expressly approximate, so the outer edge of the Metropolitan Area cannot be applied with precision.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Metropolitan Area' is load-bearing in 2-E.1, 3-E, 9-A, 12-A.1 and 4-A.2(i), and the Carlstadt (N.J.) and 150/250-mile transfer-point provisions in 22-D put pressure on its edges.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated list of covered occupations with one carve-out ('Collectors, except ...'), inviting expressio unius arguments about work not listed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-B extends coverage to 'any other operation' not expressly set forth, and 2-C to new mechanical devices, so the reach of the list is defined by other clauses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition of 'dealer' is circular and the parenthetical example is garbled, and the exception for hospitals/clubs/'other government or municipal building' is an unbounded catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It interacts with 2-A.1 (routemen) and 3-B (Publisher determines places routemen receive papers), but no direct contradiction was found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other operation, occupation or branch of work which is now being performed exclusively by employees' is a classic general catch-all sitting against the enumerated list in 2-A.1, with 'now' and 'exclusively' both undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly builds on 2-A and is invoked by 2-H.2 for new buildings, so its reach depends on how those clauses are read; 2-H.1 preserves other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, which pulls the other way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'New mechanical devices' introduced 'to perform or aid in the performance of' unit operations is broadly worded and its boundary is not fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.4 treats automated processes as something that may create excess situations, and 2-H.1 preserves other unions' mailroom jurisdiction, so exclusive operation is not absolute.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite recognition of named terminal types within the City as delivery points; nothing genuinely ambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 2-E.1 (buses/ferries/airplanes) and 22-C.b (airport pickup); no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Canada points' is a term of art defined only by function, and 'where for any reason distribution is interrupted' is broad, but the clause is short and permissive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-C addresses Canada point men's duties and is consistent; no other provision contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The final proviso ('this shall not be deemed to curtail the right to make substitution for a bus or railroad now being used') pulls against the prohibition in the same sentence, and 'existing means or methods' is undated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-E.2(h) lets a Publisher employ 'railroad, aircraft, or any other form of transportation' at will, which is in tension with the approval requirement here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence permissive grant with no undefined operative term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D expressly reinterprets 2-E.2 for The Times, but that memorandum supplements rather than contradicts this subparagraph.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Qualified, in order of seniority' is workable, though 'in accordance with Section 4-B' points to a bidding clause rather than a selection rule.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4-A.1(b) makes priority, not seniority, the measure for claiming situations, and 4-B mixes seniority and competence, so the cross-reference is imperfect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'A reasonable number of employees' is a vague quantity that the parties could read very differently.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Nothing else in the Agreement fixes the number; 4-A.4 requires competence but does not resolve the quantity.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'This article is intended only to establish terms and conditions' is a scope-limiting sentence whose interaction with the preceding grant of rights is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E freezes methods and extent of delivery absent Board approval, which sits against the freedom to 'continue and expand' work handed to an over-the-road carrier.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'As near the limits of such areas as practical' is a soft standard, and transfer points are left 'to be agreed upon by the parties.'
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (ii)-(iv) rewrites paragraph (e) for The Times with 150/250-mile rules located outside the Metropolitan Area, which cannot be squared with 'within the Metropolitan Area' here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear and specific: runs to Albany or any other designated city outside the Area are driven through by covered employees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (i) excepts common-carrier runs over 250 miles or with more than two stops, which is hard to reconcile with the unqualified through-driving rule here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: OCR damage aside, the mechanics of combination runs are described concretely; 'presently recognized exchange points' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-E's freeze on methods and extent of combined delivery and 22-A's Carlstadt arrangements bear on this, but no square conflict emerged.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conditional self-help right triggered by a 'jurisdictional dispute with another union', a term left undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-H.1 commits the Union to arbitrate jurisdictional conflicts, and 22-D (vii) has its own jurisdictional-dispute fallback, so the trigger is addressed inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any other form of transportation provided for by this contract to the extent that such forms may now be employed' is a general catch-all whose reach turns on an undated 'now'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-D Point Two (x) expressly construes paragraph (h) to bar assigning long-running runs to common carriers, and 3-E freezes methods and extent, both cutting against the free hand given here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Laid off solely as a result of' is a causation test that could be argued either way, but the sentence is short and its subject is fixed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-D.1 preserves an unqualified right to lay off for economic or business reasons, which is a familiar counterweight to 'solely as a result of' protections.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed dollar bonus for a defined triggering event; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to the 3-Q hi-lo bonus and consistent with the Section 13 wage tables; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Are or become members of the Union' is conditional but plain; the prohibition on contracting with another union is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-H.1 preserves other unions' prevailing mailroom jurisdiction, which slightly cuts against this protection but does not squarely contradict it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practice, however, excepted' is an undefined saving clause that can swallow the rule it qualifies.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Similar 'present practice' savings appear in 3-G, 12-C and 5-N, and 21-C.3 addresses home delivery franchise runs differently at The News.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Conditions and methods of operation now prevailing' is undated and undefined, and the arbitration duty is conditioned on other unions agreeing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-A's Carlstadt jurisdiction grants to the delivery department and 2-B/2-C's exclusivity claims sit against the freeze on prevailing mailroom jurisdiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Full operations commence' and 'annex or a new or additional building' are workable but not sharply bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly incorporates 2-A and 2-B, while 22-A separately negotiates jurisdiction at the new Carlstadt facility and 21-D supersedes other agreements at Newspoint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but the two protections are stated concretely; 'performing satisfactorily' is the only soft term.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.4 and 4-D deal with competence and disqualification and are broadly consistent with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The first sentence is broken ('shall be entitled to for work'), leaving the operative right — presumably to apply or shape — unstated on the face of the text.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 4-A.2 governs hiring and shaping in detail, and the Adjustment Board controls listings, so the freestanding entitlement here is hard to place.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A crisp prohibition with a named exception for foremen and assistant foremen.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 6-B expressly limits foremen's performance of Section 2 operations, and 10-A permits non-member half-day boys, both of which qualify the rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'The maximum Union security permissible under the Labor Management Relations Act ... to the extent embodied in Section 17' is a self-referential formula whose content is not fixed by the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-A.1 states the closed shop is eliminated yet reprints the old 2-L in italics, and 17-A.2 would revive it automatically, leaving the actual security level uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite membership and timing rule for regular situation holders.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.3 contemplates non-member extras and casuals paying agency fees, which is consistent; 10-A permits non-member half-day boys.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The opening clause is garbled ('employed or to be employed to an the requirements'), and 'the full shift' at time and one-half is stated without saying which shift.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same language appears verbatim in the italicized, expressly non-operative 2-L reproduced in 17-A.1, creating doubt about which text governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line prohibition on engaging helpers; plain in meaning.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 10-A/10-B expressly allow half-day boys working 'in aid of and under the direction of a route man', which is in some tension with this bar.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Detailed and mechanical: authorization, timing, remittance and hold-harmless are all specified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Weekly Checkoff letter promises to amend 2-N.1 on 60 days' notice to weekly or bi-weekly deduction, displacing the 'second pay check' rule here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short statutory-compliance clause with no operative ambiguity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parallel to 17-B's separability mechanism; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The cap is stated as a percentage of 'monthly dues' applied to a per-shift amount, which is an awkward unit mismatch but arithmetically workable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-N.1 covers regular situation holders and 2-L.2 requires their membership, so the agency-fee scheme fits the rest without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The schedule is defined by reference to 'the last notice of such schedules', an external and undated document, capped by a 46-pound limit.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-H fixes different bundle counts and weights for The Times and 21-C.2/21-D fix loads for The News, so shop schedules coexist with this general rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Requires publication of a schedule but states no substantive limit, leaving 'may be asked to carry' undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-A.4 supplies the complaint route and 21-D/22-H supply shop-specific numbers, so the framework is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain posting and furnishing obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with 4-G's list-posting duty; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unduly burdensome' and 'newspaper operational conditions warrant it' are soft standards, though they are only triggers for arbitration.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It routes to Section 16, consistent with 3-B and 3-H.1; 16-A's 30-day limit applies.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Unduly burdensome' and 'unduly difficult to serve' are vague, but they only open a grievance path rather than fix rights.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Publisher's right to set the number of dealers per route runs against the 21-D dealer-count schedules at Newspoint.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line duty stated in absolute terms ('personally supply all dealers and newsboys').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-D.2 defines Canada points; nothing contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Economic or business reasons' is the operative standard and 'as such Publisher may find necessary or desirable' is highly subjective, but 3-D.2 supplies a definition.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-E.6 waives the layoff right for Bulldog phase-outs and 3-D.4 bars automation layoffs of listed holders, so the recognized right is qualified elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: This clause exists precisely to fix the meaning of a phrase, and does so expansively ('all reasons of an economic or business character').
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defines the trigger used in 3-D.1 and reviewed by the Boards; consistent throughout.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall give employment to those regular situation holders laid off by the wholesaler' is definite, though the 15-working-day sequencing is intricate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It disclaims any modification of 3-E/3-F on methods and extent, and 12-D allocates financial benefits on the same facts, so the pieces fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The list-based protection is definite but the definition of automated systems is open-ended ('among other such automated processes'), and the 1981 list/1965 date pairing is odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 2-C claims exclusive operation of new mechanical devices while this clause treats automation as a source of excess situations; 3-D.6 tries to harmonise.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long and mechanical, but the 'excess regular situation holder' who keeps employment while his situation is bid away is a conceptually strained construct.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 20-E uses the same 'excess situation holder' device for Bulldog phase-outs with different consequences, and 4-B governs bidding.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A saving clause preserving obligations 'under Section 5-G or any other provisions', which is a general catch-all pointing back at a vague duty.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It expressly harmonises 3-D.1, 5-G and Section 16, which is itself an admission that those provisions pull in different directions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Methods and extent of direct delivery and combined delivery ... as they exist' is the contract's most elastic phrase, freezing an unspecified state of affairs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 3-F gives the Publisher a free hand on new routes, 2-E.2(d)/(h) allow expansion and discontinuance, and the 'Clarification of Method and Extent' letter adds a subcontracting gloss.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'New sections or new routes' is undefined and the freedom given is broad, but the sentence is otherwise clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is the express counterpart to 3-E's freeze, and the line between an existing and a 'new' route is where those two clauses meet.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Present practices' is undated and undefined, and 'good cause shown' is a soft standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-C repeats this clause almost verbatim, an unexplained duplication between Sections 3 and 12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Undue hardship or hazard', 'excessive work tasks' and 'insofar as practicable' are open-textured standards that cannot be applied from the words alone.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Heaters/Bostrum Seats letter promises only that existing under-the-seat heaters be maintained and new trucks equipped, which is narrower than the flat 30-day requirement here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The amount reads '$20,000, $50,000 beginning January 1, 1982' with no connector, and coverage is limited to death or injury 'resulting from assaults or other criminal conduct' — a general phrase after a specific one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 22-G governs Times group life insurance and 13-H the Welfare Fund; no direct conflict, but overlapping benefit sources are addressed inconsistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain management right to operate day or night shifts, tied to the wage scales.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-A and 5-B define the day and night shift periods and 13-A sets the differentiated rates, so the reference is well anchored.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Shall make every effort' and 'in so far as that may be practicable' are aspirational, and the clause then disclaims the very obligation it appears to create.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 5-I requires double time for Sunday advance-section work, so the overtime this clause tries to eliminate is separately priced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Then fair value' and 'no longer is fit for use' are soft, but the sixty-day option and the anti-discrimination proviso are concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The grandfathering of 'existing arrangements' cuts against the flat prohibition in the first sentence, but the clause resolves that itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is badly mangled and the key operative term 'extra crew' is undefined, while the paste/bill-posting carve-out is an unexplained exception.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 21-D.V(c) expressly disapplies the 'extra crew' requirements of this section to commercial work at Newspoint, confirming that its reach was contested.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense most-favoured-employer clause turning on 'any other terms or conditions more favorable', a comparison the words do not tell you how to make.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 12-A.1 requires wholesalers to be under Union agreement and 3-M's escape valve routes to the Boards; the Pension/Welfare parity letter uses a similar and equally soft comparison.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear supremacy rule for the contract over internal rules of either party.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 17-C's 'spirit as well as the letter' and 17-B's separability address the same terrain consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Best efforts collectively and individually to promote the business and interests' is a vague and unmeasurable obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 16-N's no-strike clause and 17-C's spirit-and-letter clause cover the same cooperative ground without conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Immediate family' is expressly defined by an enumerated list closing with 'legal dependents as defined by the Internal Revenue Code', which is a general catch-all after specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 13-K paid leave and 13-B vacation credit rules address absences separately; the proviso that the three days fall in the scheduled work week is self-contained.
